record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.context_brief: Operator algebras with shifts and summation
record.original_question: Develop a theory of operator algebras that contains both shift operators and summation operators, analogous to the integro-differential operator algebras of Regensburger and Rosenkranz. Within that theory, explain algebraically why the right-hand side of a creative telescoping relation often vanishes for binomial sums.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2 Develop a theory of operator algebras including shift as well as summation operators, analogous to the theory of Regensburger and Rosenkranz. In this theory, find an algebraic explanation why the right hand side of a creative telescoping relation often vanishes for binomial sums.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Regensburger and Rosenkranz developed a theory of integro-differential algebras: a commutative algebra A over a field equipped with a derivation D and a right-inverse integration operator I (so D∘I = id), together with axioms (such as the differential Baxter / integration-by-parts identity) governing their interaction; this theory yields a noncommutative algebra of integro-differential operators that captures, in a purely algebraic way, identities such as the fundamental theorem of calculus and boundary evaluations.

In the discrete setting, the relevant operators are the forward shift S, acting on sequences by (S·f)(n) = f(n+1), and a summation operator Σ which is a right-inverse of the difference Δ = S − I, i.e. ΔΣ = id, corresponding to indefinite summation. A creative telescoping relation for a bivariate sequence F(n,k) is an identity of the form
   P(n, S_n)·F(n,k) = Δ_k G(n,k),
where P is a nonzero operator polynomial in n and the shift S_n acting only in the variable n, and G(n,k) is a "certificate" expressible from F. Summing over k in an appropriate range yields a recurrence for the sum T(n) = Σ_k F(n,k); the right-hand side telescopes and is, for many binomial sums, identically zero after the summation bounds are taken into account.

Problem. Construct a theory of noncommutative operator algebras containing both shift operators S_i (in possibly several variables) and summation operators Σ_i which are right-inverses of the corresponding difference operators Δ_i, axiomatised in a manner directly analogous to the integro-differential algebras of Regensburger and Rosenkranz (with summation-by-parts identities playing the role of integration-by-parts, and appropriate "evaluation" or "boundary" linear functionals). Within this framework, give a purely algebraic explanation of the phenomenon that for binomial (and more generally hypergeometric) summands F(n,k), the right-hand side Δ_k G(n,k) of the creative telescoping relation, once summed over k, evaluates to zero — i.e. derive the vanishing of these boundary/telescoped contributions as a consequence of the axioms of the algebra rather than as a case-by-case computation.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the original problem statement and related work on integro-differential algebras (Regensburger–Rosenkranz) and on creative telescoping for binomial sums (e.g. Bostan–Lairez–Salvy on multiple binomial sums, and Chen–Koutschan style frameworks), but no source claims to have constructed the requested shift+summation operator-algebra analogue together with an algebraic explanation of the vanishing of the telescoping right-hand side for binomial sums. The status is therefore best described as unknown / apparently still open.
